items: Block/completion/reopen/supersede events are core user-facing backbone events.
Promotion blocked/promoted/revoked events are core user-facing backbone events.
Graph patch requested/applied/generation updated events are core user-facing backbone events.
Restore required/failed/completed events are core user-facing backbone events.
Threshold crossed/account switched/account exhausted events are core user-facing backbone events.
Tab badges must remain sparse and purposeful.
Progress badge should represent meaningful attention/action-required count.
Other tabs should use targeted counts or dot badges rather than noisy unread-style counters.
Unresolved conditions remain on operational surfaces.
Resolved conditions move to History.
Recently resolved major items may linger briefly in summary surfaces.
Normal resolved operational items default to about 15 minutes.
Major resolved items default to dismissal or up to 24 hours.
Future controls should be policy-level, not per-alert micro-configuration.
Resolved means underlying condition changed.
Dismissed means presentation hidden/acknowledged while condition may still exist.
Active blockers must not be dismissible in ways that imply unblocked state.
Acknowledged is distinct from resolved and dismissed.
Acknowledged applies to advisory/minor/non-blocking concerns explicitly seen/accepted by user.
Acknowledgement should reduce operational noise while preserving traceability.
Blockers requiring real action must not be acknowledgeable as a substitute for resolution.
Concern is a first-class record, not embedded-only review/alert metadata.
Concern record should include identity, scope, severity, category, owner, lifecycle state, and summary/meaning.
Concern record should link to evidence, artifacts, history, and source records.
Concern record should include visibility/attention flags.
Concern lifecycle states include active, acknowledged, resolved, and dismissed.
Canonical concerns are created by runtime, package overseer, seam overseer, corroboration outcomes, and graph patch/state-transition logic.
Workers can nominate findings but should not mint canonical concerns directly.
Persistent underlying issues should update/escalate/downgrade existing concerns instead of creating duplicates.
Resolution must track underlying truth changes, not presentation-only changes.
All major surfaces should project a shared concern model rather than local variants.
Progress is the operational attention projection.
Seams is the integration/governance projection.
Evidence is the proof-backed concern projection.
History is the concern lifecycle timeline projection.
Ledger is the exact structured concern-record projection.
User-facing concern actions should remain narrow: open/focus/open evidence/open history/open ledger.
Acknowledge and dismiss actions should be exposed only where allowed.
Open resolution thread is an allowed user-facing concern action.
Approve/reject actions should only appear at true manual/HITL boundaries.
Runtime/overseer actions remain mostly non-generic GUI actions: request corroboration, route to remediation, request graph patch, mutate severity/owner, merge/split, and true resolution.
Side inspectors should stay summary-oriented and action-light.
Heavy/high-consequence actions and dense records belong in full-record views.
Orchestrator widgets should consume stable shared projections, not raw event streams or bespoke queries.
Widget shell needs identity/type, scope, filter/sort/display config, and projection reference.

Required projection families include run, seam, package, node, promotion, lane/worktree, concern, account/usage pressure, recent major events, corroboration, recovery, and overseer activity summaries.
Run/seam/concern/account-pressure/recent-major-events summaries should be reusable across Orchestrator, Dashboard, and Projects.
Operationally dense summaries should remain primarily Orchestrator-focused.
Primary projection updates should be event-driven; manual refresh/tab reopen are secondary.
Projection health states include current, refreshing, stale, and failed.
Projection health degradation should mint a real concern when it threatens trust in blocked/promotion/recovery/patch/account-pressure truth.
Truth-changing actions require fresh-enough projection state; observational/navigation/export actions generally remain safe.
Gating UI should state what is stale, why it matters, and what user can do next.
Under stale projections, degrade to direct record-backed inspection.
Ledger/direct records are trust anchors under degraded projection health.
Only current and generation-matched direct records should be action-capable.
Most trustworthy action-capable direct records are promotion records, graph patch records with state transition reports, recovery/restore records, and concern records for acknowledge/dismiss.
Action-capable direct record views should explicitly show currentness, generation match, superseded status, and actionable status.
Each tab needs role-appropriate filters.
Orchestrator should support at least per-project saved views for tabs/filters/sort/grouping/widget layout.
Default sorting: Seams by most operationally problematic first; History newest first; Ledger newest first.
Dashboard is summary/urgency/entry points; Orchestrator is operational depth; Projects is richer multi-project summary management.
Project cards should show compact orchestrator/attention/usage pressure state and one primary blocked owner/reason when blocked.
Projects page shows coarse account/usage pressure summary.
Dashboard shows cross-project pressure with operational importance.
Orchestrator shows execution-specific provider/account pressure context.
Usage page should include account-level breakdown, role usage view, and switch history, while full Usage-page redesign is out of current thread scope.
Multi-account belongs with provider/model setup, not isolated orchestrator-only settings.
Major settings groupings include Providers & Models, Execution Identity, Governance, Workers, Recovery, and HITL.

Scope hierarchy: App/Global defaults, Project as primary policy owner, Seam feature-level overrides, Package local execution/recovery overrides, Node rare targeted overrides, Actor/Role cross-cutting policy, Runtime-only as computed truth.
UI should explicitly display Inherited, Overridden, and Effective without requiring separate resolution/inheritance modal.
Node Graph tab should include graph canvas and right-side detail inspector.

Node detail should expose requested/effective provider-model-effort-persona-account, usage/token/cost, worker policy, retry/review/promotion state, lane/worktree/snapshot state, and linked evidence/artifacts.
Evidence/artifact links from node detail should navigate to Evidence tab with relevant item selected.
Important objects/events should be deep-linkable across Progress, Seams, Node Graph, Evidence, History, and Ledger.
Cross-tab navigation should preserve/filter/select target context rather than only switching tabs.
Usage tracking is already heavily documented, with strongest ownership in usage-feature documentation plus supporting storage and GUI planning docs.
Usage is already treated as first-class cross-surface concern, not a side feature.

Existing docs already assume warning thresholds, platform quota visibility, rate-limit/reset countdown surfaces, project-scoped usage storage, dashboard widgets, and orchestrator/runtime event persistence.
